_note: Original practice items written for the Classic EDU Suite CBT bank. Not reproduced from any past paper. Syllabus-aligned to JAMB Physics.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N), where 1 N = 1 kg m/s².
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; the others have magnitude only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 4 m/s² for 5 seconds. Find its final velocity.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 4 m/s² for 5 seconds. What distance does it cover?
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Calculate the force required to give a mass of 10 kg an acceleration of 2 m/s².
questions.explanation: From Newton's second law, F = ma = 10 × 2 = 20 N.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Find the momentum of a body of mass 5 kg moving with a velocity of 4 m/s.
questions.explanation: Momentum p = mv = 5 × 4 = 20 kg m/s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A force of 10 N acts on a body for 3 seconds. Calculate the impulse.
questions.explanation: Impulse = Ft = 10 × 3 = 30 Ns.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A force of 50 N moves a body through a distance of 4 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done.
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance = 50 × 4 = 200 J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A machine does 600 J of work in 5 seconds. Calculate its power.
questions.explanation: Power = work/time = 600/5 = 120 W.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Calculate the kinetic energy of a body of mass 2 kg moving at 3 m/s.
questions.explanation: K.E. = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A body of mass 5 kg is raised to a height of 10 m. Calculate its potential energy. [g = 10 m/s²]
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A stone is released from rest and falls freely for 3 seconds. Find its velocity just before impact. [g = 10 m/s²]
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A body of mass 200 g occupies a volume of 50 cm³. Calculate its density.
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 200/50 = 4 g/cm³.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A force of 200 N acts normally on an area of 0.5 m². Calculate the pressure exerted.
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = 200/0.5 = 400 Pa.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 2 m in water of density 1000 kg/m³. [g = 10 m/s²]
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A body wholly or partially immersed in a fluid experiences an upthrust equal to
options: the weight of the fluid displaced
the volume of the fluid displaced
questions.explanation: This is Archimedes' principle: the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Which statement best expresses Hooke's law?
options: Force is proportional to the square of the extension
Within the elastic limit, extension is directly proportional to the applied force
Stress is inversely proportional to strain
Extension is proportional to the length of the wire
questions.explanation: Hooke's law holds only up to the elastic limit, where extension ∝ force.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A load of 20 N produces an extension of 4 cm in a spring. Calculate the force constant of the spring.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Calculate the heat required to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water by 10 °C. [specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kg K]
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Calculate the heat required to melt 0.5 kg of ice at 0 °C. [specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg]
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A gas occupies 3 litres at a pressure of 2 atmospheres. What volume will it occupy at 1 atmosphere if the temperature is constant?
questions.explanation: By Boyle's law, P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = (2 × 3)/1 = 6 litres.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Charles' law states that at constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is
options: proportional to the square of its temperature
directly proportional to its absolute temperature
questions.explanation: V ∝ T at constant pressure, where T is measured in kelvin.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Heat is transferred through liquids and gases mainly by
questions.explanation: The warmer, less dense fluid rises and cooler fluid sinks, setting up convection currents.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Mercury is preferred to water as a thermometric liquid mainly because it
options: does not wet glass and expands uniformly
is a poor conductor of heat
questions.explanation: Mercury is opaque, does not cling to the glass and expands regularly over a wide range.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A wave of frequency 50 Hz has a wavelength of 4 m. Calculate its speed.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Calculate the period of a wave whose frequency is 25 Hz.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Which of the following cannot travel through a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium to propagate.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A boy claps his hands near a wall and hears the echo 2 seconds later. How far is he from the wall? [speed of sound = 340 m/s]
questions.explanation: The sound covers 2 × distance in 2 s, so distance = (340 × 2)/2 = 340 m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: When light is reflected from a plane mirror, the angle of incidence is
options: equal to the angle of reflection
questions.explanation: The first law of reflection: the angles of incidence and reflection are equal.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A ray of light passes from air into a medium with an angle of incidence of 60° and an angle of refraction of 30°. Calculate the refractive index of the medium.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels
options: from a less dense to a denser medium at any angle
from a denser to a less dense medium below the critical angle
along the normal between two media
from a denser to a less dense medium at an angle greater than the critical angle
questions.explanation: Both conditions are required: denser to less dense, and incidence beyond the critical angle.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: An object is placed beyond 2F in front of a converging lens. The image formed is
options: real, upright and the same size
questions.explanation: Beyond 2F the image falls between F and 2F on the other side, and is real, inverted and smaller.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: An object 15 cm from a converging lens forms a real image 30 cm from the lens. Calculate the focal length.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A potential difference of 12 V is applied across a 3 Ω resistor. Calculate the current flowing.
questions.explanation: From Ohm's law, I = V/R = 12/3 = 4 A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are connected in series. Find the effective resistance.
questions.explanation: In series, resistances simply add: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A 6 Ω resistor and a 3 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. Find the effective resistance.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: An electric heater rated 2000 W is used for 3 hours. Calculate the energy consumed in kilowatt-hours.
questions.explanation: Energy = power × time = 2 kW × 3 h = 6 kWh.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A cell of e.m.f. 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to an external resistor of 5 Ω. Calculate the current in the circuit.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: The main purpose of a fuse in an electrical circuit is to
options: melt and break the circuit when the current is excessive
increase the current in the circuit
questions.explanation: A fuse is a deliberately weak link that melts before the wiring or appliance is damaged.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: The direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor is given by
questions.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of force, not of the field around a conductor.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A transformer steps 240 V down to 12 V. If the primary coil has 1000 turns, how many turns has the secondary coil?
questions.explanation: Ns/Np = Vs/Vp, so Ns = 1000 × 12/240 = 50 turns.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced e.m.f. is proportional to the
options: square of the number of turns
rate of change of magnetic flux linkage
questions.explanation: It is the rate of change of flux linkage, not the flux itself, that induces an e.m.f.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: An a.c. generator converts
questions.explanation: A coil is rotated in a magnetic field, so mechanical work becomes electrical energy.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: Two capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in parallel. Find the effective capacitance.
questions.explanation: Capacitors in parallel add directly: 2 + 3 = 5 μF.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: The minimum energy required to eject an electron from the surface of a metal is called the
questions.explanation: The work function is an energy; the threshold frequency is the corresponding frequency.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: An alpha particle is identical to
questions.explanation: An alpha particle consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons, which is a helium nucleus.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: A radioactive sample of mass 80 g has a half-life of 5 days. What mass remains after 15 days?
questions.explanation: 15 days is 3 half-lives: 80 → 40 → 20 → 10 g.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: How many neutrons are there in an atom of uranium with mass number 238 and atomic number 92?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 238 − 92 = 146.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: X-rays are produced when
options: a radioactive nucleus emits an alpha particle
visible light is passed through a prism
an electric current flows through an electrolyte
fast-moving electrons are suddenly stopped by a metal target
questions.explanation: The sudden deceleration of high-energy electrons at the target releases X-radiation.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question: The energy of a quantum of radiation of frequency f is given by
questions.explanation: Planck's relation gives E = hf, where h is Planck's constant.
questions.subject: Physics
